title: Persian Solar Hijri Calendar
intro: The Solar Hijri calendar is a solar calendar used for civil dates in Iran and related traditions. Nowruz, the first day of its year, falls close to the northern spring equinox.
structure: Twelve months form a common year of 365 days or a leap year of 366 days. The first six months contain 31 days, the next five contain 30 days, and Esfand contains 29 days in a common year or 30 in a leap year.
example: 1 Farvardin usually corresponds to 20 or 21 March in Gregorian notation; the exact correspondence depends on the year and calendar rule.
history: Modern civil Solar Hijri month lengths were standardised in the twentieth century. Nowruz has a much longer cultural history. Official conventions have varied across countries and historical periods; the modern month structure cannot be assumed to apply to older Persian dates.
model: The provider uses an ICU-compatible arithmetic cycle, not lunar sightings or direct observation of the equinox. The epoch is JDN 1948320. The base leap rule is positive remainder (25*y+11) modulo 33 < 8; the maintained correction table designates exceptions as common years and the following years as leap years. The year-start offset is 365*(y-1)+floor((8*y+21)/33), reduced by one when y>1502 and the previous year is a correction year. Add the epoch, the cumulative month length and d-1 to obtain JDN. The exact exception table is in the referenced implementation.
limits: The implemented arithmetic is not a reconstruction of historical Iranian month lengths before 1304 AP (1925 CE), nor a blanket guarantee of every equinox-based civil decision.
